title: A symphony orchestra playing without a conductor
summary: A Russian woman takes them to hear a 110-piece orchestra playing Tchaikovsky in a circle with no leader.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, another a very wonderful thing. There was a lady, she was a very fine Russian Jewish woman and she spoke English very fluently. And so she said, 'I want to show you something that you don't have in your democracies.' And she took us to the symphony hall. And in this symphony hall, there were 110 musicians. It was a symphony orchestra. And they were all sitting in a circle without a leader. And without a leader they played Tschaikovsky, they played Borodin, and Rimsky-Korsakov. Symphonies.

They played these things. And without a leader. And we sat up all night trying to figure how it was done. But the nearest we got to it was that each soloist was the leader. That's what we figured it was, but we can't even prove that. We was guessing at that. But they actually did that for the first time. A hundred and ten men played. All in a circle. They sat in a circle facing each other. And they played -- now that was one of the things that we had never seen before.
